questions.stem: Bihu is the most famous and widely celebrated traditional folk dance of which Northeastern Indian state?
questions.explanation: Bihu is an indigenous folk dance from Assam related to the Bihu festival, performed by young men and women. It is characterised by brisk dance steps and rapid hand movements.

questions.stem: The Cheraw dance, highly famous for its rhythmic stepping and commonly referred to as the 'Bamboo Dance', belongs to which state?
questions.explanation: Cheraw is a traditional cultural dance performed in Mizoram. It consists of mostly six to eight people holding pairs of bamboo staves on the ground, tapping them in rhythmic beats while women dance by stepping in and out of the bamboo.

questions.stem: The unique Hojagiri dance, where women intricately balance earthen pitchers and props on their heads, is a traditional folk dance primarily performed by the Reang community in which state?
questions.explanation: Hojagiri is a famous folk dance of Tripura, performed exclusively by women of the Reang (Bru) clan. The dance involves complex balancing acts using bottles, earthen lamps, and plates, while only moving the lower half of the body.

questions.stem: The Nongkrem dance is an essential religious harvest festival dance performed specifically by the Khasi tribe in which Northeastern state?
questions.explanation: Nongkrem is a prominent five-day religious festival of the Khasi tribe of Meghalaya. The dance is performed to appease the all-powerful Goddess Ka Blei Synshar for a rich bumper harvest and prosperity.

questions.stem: Which famous harvest festival dance is enthusiastically performed by the Garo tribe of Meghalaya, and is often popularly known as the 'Festival of 100 Drums'?
questions.explanation: Wangala is the most significant post-harvest festival of the Garo tribe in Meghalaya. It is a thanksgiving ceremony to Misi Saljong, the Sun God. The rhythmic beating of 100 traditional long cylindrical drums (Nagara) is its hallmark.

questions.stem: The traditional and ancient martial arts dance form strictly known as 'Thang-Ta' originates from the rich cultural heritage of which specific Northeastern state?
questions.explanation: Thang-Ta (meaning 'Sword and Spear') is an exclusive martial art form of Manipur, created by the Meitei people. It is practiced both as a combat technique and a highly choreographed ritualistic dance.

questions.stem: The 'Ponung' dance is an important religious folk dance performed almost exclusively by the women of the Adi tribe to pray for a good harvest and welfare in which state?
questions.explanation: Ponung is a popular folk dance of the Adi tribe of Arunachal Pradesh. It is a joyous dance performed only by young women and girls in a circle, holding each other's hands, led by a single male singer (Miri).

questions.stem: The 'Bagurumba', popularly called the 'butterfly dance' due to its graceful swaying movements, is the traditional folk dance of which tribal community of Assam?

options.option_text: Mising tribe of upper Assam riverine areas
Bodo tribe of the Brahmaputra plains
Karbi tribe of the Assam hill districts
Dimasa tribe of the North Cachar Hills

questions.explanation: Bagurumba is the traditional folk dance of the Bodo tribe — the largest plains tribal group of Assam — performed during the Bwisagu festival. The Mising tribe is a common distractor because they also inhabit the Brahmaputra valley, but their signature dance is the Dobur Uie, not Bagurumba.

questions.stem: The 'Shad Suk Mynsiem', meaning 'Dance of the Joyful Hearts', is a spring thanksgiving dance performed exclusively by unmarried women and young men of which community in Meghalaya?

options.option_text: Rabha community of the border foothills

questions.explanation: Shad Suk Mynsiem is a Khasi spring festival dance held annually in April at Shillong. The Garo community's signature festival dance is Wangala, and the Jaintia community celebrates Behdienkhlam — both are frequent wrong choices as they are all Meghalaya tribes.

questions.stem: The 'Lai Haraoba', considered the oldest surviving ritual performance of Manipur, is enacted to propitiate which category of deities central to the pre-Vaishnavite Meitei faith?

options.option_text: Vaishnavite deities of the Meitei royal court
Umang Lai — sylvan deities of the Meitei faith
Buddhist deities of the Theravada tradition
Tantric deities worshipped by the Naga tribes

questions.explanation: Lai Haraoba ('merry-making of the gods') propitiates the Umang Lai — sylvan or forest deities of the indigenous Meitei religion, Sanamahism. The Vaishnavite option is the strongest distractor because Vaishnavism later co-existed with and absorbed elements of Lai Haraoba, but the ritual itself predates Vaishnavite influence in Manipur.

questions.stem: The 'Khuallam' dance, featuring performers in colourful robes carrying gongs and bamboo props, is traditionally the centrepiece of which festival in Mizoram?

options.option_text: Mim Kut festival honouring the maize harvest
Pawl Kut festival celebrating a bumper harvest
Chapchar Kut festival held in early spring season
Thalfavang Kut festival observed in the autumn

questions.explanation: Khuallam is performed during Chapchar Kut, Mizoram's largest spring festival celebrated after jhum (shifting cultivation) land clearance. The Cheraw (bamboo dance) is also performed at Chapchar Kut. Pawl Kut and Mim Kut are harvest festivals — a common source of confusion because all three are prominent Mizo festivals.

questions.stem: The 'Bardo Chham', a masked dance depicting the triumph of good over evil using elaborate Buddhist iconography, is primarily performed by the Monpa community and linked to which North-East state?

options.option_text: Sikkim, home to Rumtek and Pemayangtse monasteries
Arunachal Pradesh, associated with Tawang monastery
Nagaland, where Tibetan Buddhist festivals are held
Manipur, homeland of the classical Manipuri style

questions.explanation: Bardo Chham is native to the Monpa tribal community of Arunachal Pradesh, centred around Tawang — India's largest Buddhist monastery after Rumtek. Sikkim is the most tempting wrong answer as it also hosts prominent Cham masked dances at its monasteries, but Bardo Chham is specifically attributed to Arunachal Pradesh.

questions.stem: In Manipur's dance tradition, the 'Pung Cholom' is the male acrobatic drum dance. Which dance form is its direct female counterpart, performed by women who play kartal (hand cymbals) with synchronised acrobatic footwork?

options.option_text: Nupa Cholom (Kartal Cholom) performed by Meitei women
Khamba Thoibi performed at the Lai Haraoba festival
Thougal Jagoi performed during royal Meitei rituals
Laho dance performed by Meitei women of Imphal valley

questions.explanation: Nupa Cholom (also called Kartal Cholom — 'nupa' meaning female in Meitei) is the female counterpart to Pung Cholom, where women play hand cymbals in synchronised acrobatic sequences. Khamba Thoibi is the strongest distractor as it is also a celebrated Meitei dance, but it narrates a folk legend involving a shepherd youth and a princess rather than being an instrument-based counterpart.

questions.stem: The 'Ojapali' is a semi-classical performing art of Assam blending song, recitation, and dance. Its 'Byah Ojapali' variant specifically narrates the Manasamangal cycle, dedicated to propitiation of which deity?

options.option_text: Bishahari (Manasa) — the serpent goddess of Assam
Kamakhya — the tantric Shakti goddess of Nilachal
Durga — the principal Shakta deity of the autumn puja
Narayana — the Vaishnavite deity of the Sattra system

questions.explanation: The Byah Ojapali narrates stories from the Manasamangal — epics centred on Manasa, also called Bishahari, the goddess of serpents worshipped widely in rural Assam and Bengal. Kamakhya is the most tempting wrong answer because she is Assam's most iconic goddess and a major pilgrimage site, but Ojapali's Byah tradition is specifically tied to Manasa worship, not to the Kamakhya tradition.
